readingsEntry.title: Meter readings
readingsEntry.subtitle: Quick on-site entry — all meters at a glance.

empty.title: No meters
empty.text: Central entry is only available for cumulative meters (gas, electricity, water, district heating). Heating oil/pellets track consumption via deliveries, not meter readings.

hint.lower: Note: value is lower than the last reading ({min}). That's fine for a meter swap etc.

noMeters.title: No meters yet
noMeters.text: Add a {label} meter via the meter management.

kpi.co2AvoidedTitle: Simplified model: kWh fed in × grid-mix CO₂ factor. PV life-cycle not included.

contractsTable.emptyText: Add a contract to track advances, tariff prices, bonuses and balance.

monthlyTable.colHddTitle: Heating degree days — sum of daily differences between heating limit and outdoor temperature

tank.noCapacity: No tank capacity set — enter it on the meter to see the stock curve.
tank.modelNote: Stock is modelled from initial stock + deliveries − HDD-weighted consumption; it is an estimate, not a tank gauge.

chart.alt: Bar chart: monthly consumption and average temperature

deliveryModal.validation: Date and a positive quantity are required.

contracts.title: {label} · Contracts

delivery.bannerText: Unlike gas, electricity, water or district heating, there is no supply contract with working and base prices here. Costs come directly from each delivery/tank invoice (quantity × price per {unit}, or the recorded total amount). A tariff comparison with shadow contracts also does not apply to {label}.

contracts.metersWarning: Add meters first before creating contracts.

row.setStartFirst: Please set the contract start date first

modal.validationHalfRows: Please complete or clear half-empty rows

special.title: Special payments
special.hint: Refund, surcharge or additional advance payment. “Affecting” also adjusts the future monthly advance.

info.title: Multiple meters per utility
info.text: — e.g. hot water & heating (gas) or peak/off-peak & wallbox (electricity). Each meter has its own device history (meter swaps are calculated without loss) and can carry its own contracts.
info.topologyText: Sub-meters are subtracted from the parent meter; groups combine several meters in the dashboard.

deleteGroup.title: Dissolve group?
deleteGroup.message: Dissolve group “{name}”? The assigned meters are kept and are only removed from the group.

deleteMeter.title: Delete meter?
deleteMeter.message: Delete meter “{name}” and its device history? Readings and contracts must be removed first.

modal.name: Name *
modal.namePlaceholder: e.g. hot water, heating, peak, wallbox
modal.parentHint: This meter's consumption is subtracted from the parent meter.

replace.title: Meter swap: {name}
replace.intro: Closes the currently open device with a final reading and creates a new device. Consumption across the swap is calculated correctly automatically — no more “negative consumption” after a swap.

import.title: Import readings: {name}
import.intro: Imports readings from a CSV file directly into the meter {name}. An existing reading on the same date is overwritten and reported in the result.
import.formatHint: Separator ; or , · date DD.MM.YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD · decimal comma allowed · columns note and estimated optional · a header row is detected automatically.
import.dropZone: Drop a CSV file here or click to select
import.dropZoneAria: Select a CSV file or drop it here

mergeModal.title: Merge meters
mergeModal.intro: Merge several meters into one group — e.g. off-peak + peak electricity or several wallboxes. The group combines consumption in the dashboard; the individual meters are kept.
mergeModal.needTwo: Please select at least two meters
mergeModal.needName: Please provide a group name or choose an existing group

lang.title: 🌐 Language / Sprache
lang.hint: Interface language. The change takes effect immediately.
lang.label: Language

physical.title: Physical constants
physical.hint: Conversion and heating-degree-day base — affect all analyses.

co2.title: CO₂ emission factors
co2.hint: Grams of CO₂ per consumption unit, for the emission estimate.

billing.title: Billing cycle
billing.hint: Annual settlement date per utility (format DD-MM, e.g. 01-01 for 1 January, 15-04 for 15 April). Determines how far the balance of open contracts is projected; contracts with a maintained end date still use that end.

contractReminders.title: Contract reminders
contractReminders.hint: Days before contract end from which the contract overview warns. Three levels — early warning to last day.

water.title: Water reference values
water.hint: Household size, per-capita reference and the bands of the saving index.

regression.title: Regression & forecast
regression.hint: Filters for the regression basis and parameters of the forecast model.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.hint: Display scope and thresholds of the overview.

building.title: Building & efficiency
building.hint: Reference values for the efficiency class (kWh/m²·a) and the heating-energy benchmark.

delivery.title: Energy sources (delivery)
delivery.hint: Energy content of delivery-based fuels and the tank warning threshold.

remindersRec.title: Reminders & recommendations
remindersRec.hint: Thresholds for due status and the recommendation engine.

location.title: Location (Open-Meteo)
location.hint: Coordinates for the weather sync of the temperature series.

gas_conversion_factor.label: Gas conversion factor
gas_conversion_factor.hint: Calorific value × state number per gas bill.

hdd_base_temp.label: HDD base temperature
hdd_base_temp.hint: Heating limit — days below count as heating days.

wasser_sparindex_gut.label: Saving index — good up to
wasser_sparindex_gut.hint: Index ≤ this value is considered unremarkable.

wasser_sparindex_warnung.label: Saving index — warning from
wasser_sparindex_warnung.hint: Index ≥ this value indicates saving potential.

segmented_split_mode.label: Segment breakpoint
segmented_split_mode.hint: auto = fitted from data, fixed = fixed HDD value below.

wohnflaeche_m2.label: Living area
wohnflaeche_m2.hint: Heated area — denominator of the efficiency metric.

gebaeudetyp.label: Building type
gebaeudetyp.hint: efh = detached, rh = terraced, mfh = multi-family, whg = flat.

delivery_baseload_share.label: Base-load share distribution
delivery_baseload_share.hint: Share of consumption as weather-independent base load (rest HDD-weighted).

activeUtils.title: 🧩 Active utilities
activeUtils.hint: Only checked utilities appear in the sidebar, dashboard and annual report. Data of inactive utilities is kept.

pdf.title: 📄 PDF annual report
pdf.hint: Multi-page report with overview, efficiency class, consumption tables per utility and open recommendations.

export.title: 📤 Data export (CSV)
export.hint: Tabular export for Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets — semicolon-separated, UTF-8 with BOM, German decimal comma. Complements the full JSON backup below.
export.monthlyHint: Consumption, cost, advance and balance per month.
export.readingsHint: Cumulative types: raw readings. Heating oil/pellets: fuel deliveries (one row per delivery).
export.temperaturesHint: Daily min / avg / max values of the whole series.

backup.title: 💾 Backup & restore
backup.hint: Full JSON backup (format v3.0) — contains all utilities, meters, contracts, temperatures and settings, re-importable.
backup.demoHint: “Load demo data” imports a complete example dataset — ideal for trying out an empty Energietracker. If data already exists, you are warned first and a snapshot is created automatically.
backup.demoUnavailable: Demo data is not available in this installation.
backup.demoConfirmMsg: Data already exists. The import overwrites it. Beforehand, a safety snapshot of your current data is created automatically, which you can restore at any time.
backup.importConfirmMsg: Warning: existing data will be overwritten. Before the import, the app automatically stores a safety snapshot of your current data under data/backups/pre-restore-… — if the import doesn't look as expected, you can restore this snapshot.
backup.migrateHint: Upload an old v0.9.0 backup (JSON with version: "2.1"). The backup is analysed before writing; then you choose between Replace (overwrite everything) or Merge (add new IDs only). In both cases a safety snapshot of the current data is created automatically beforehand.

ha.title: 🏠 Home Assistant integration
ha.intro: Let Home Assistant send your meter readings to the Energietracker automatically — you no longer maintain them by hand. Home Assistant provides the values, the Energietracker handles contracts, costs and forecasts. Guide: docs/HOME-ASSISTANT.md.
ha.tokenHint: Protects the push endpoint /api/ingest. As long as no token is set, the API stays open (intended for the local network only). Once a token exists, Home Assistant must send it along.
ha.revealLabel: Token (copy now — it will not be shown again):
ha.aliasHint: Give each meter an easy-to-remember alias (e.g. electricity_house) that you enter in Home Assistant — more convenient than the internal ID. Allowed: letters, digits, _ . -. Leave empty = no alias.
ha.configHint: Add this to your configuration.yaml and adjust URL/token. A complete automation with examples is in docs/HOME-ASSISTANT.md.
ha.genConfirmMsg: A new token is generated and shown only ONCE. Any existing token becomes invalid.
ha.revokeConfirmMsg: After revoking, the push endpoint is reachable without a token again (open mode). Home Assistant automations with the old token will fail.
ha.clipboardUnavailable: Clipboard not available — please select manually

migrationDialog.title: Migration from v0.9.0
migrationDialog.detected: Detected v0.9.0 backup format {version}. Data has been translated to the current schema (not yet written).
migrationDialog.candidatesHint: — model as device swap after the import?
migrationDialog.candidatesNote: After the import, model them under Meters & devices → Meter swap (or API: POST /api/utility/{u}/meters/{id}/replace-device).
migrationDialog.replaceDesc: — existing data is deleted and replaced by the backup. A safety snapshot of the current data is stored under data/backups/ automatically beforehand.
migrationDialog.mergeDesc: — only readings/contracts with a new ID are added. Existing data is kept. Temperature days are only added if the date does not yet exist.

reminders.title: Reminders & maintenance
reminders.subtitle: Recurring maintenance, calibration deadlines and delivery reminders.

temperatures.title: 🌡️ Temperature
temperatures.formatHint: Format: DD.MM.YYYY"avg"min"max (e.g. 15.01.2024"4.2"-1.0"7.1). Values in °C, double quotes as separator.
temperatures.dropZone: Drop a file here or click to select
temperatures.dropZoneAria: Select a CSV file or drop it here

chart.alt: Line chart: monthly minimum, average and maximum temperature

temperatures.locHint: Default: Leipzig. Used for the Open-Meteo sync.

recommendations.title: Recommendations
recommendations.subtitle: Statistical hints from your own data — no external sources.

r1.title: {label} {ym}: weather-adjusted {pct} % above average
r1.detail: In {ym} the weather-adjusted consumption was {pct} % above your average — and it wasn't colder. An appliance or heating check may be worthwhile.

r2.title: {label}: rising trend {pct} %/year
r2.detail: The weather-adjusted consumption is rising by about {pct} % per year — a gradual decline. Check whether appliances are ageing or usage habits have changed.

r3.title: {label} {year}: high summer consumption
r3.detail: In July {year} consumption was {pct} % of the January value. For pure space heating this should be much lower — likely inefficient hot-water preparation.

r4.title: {label} {ym}: statistical anomaly
r4.detail: Consumption in {ym} deviates unusually strongly ({sigma}σ) and is not explained by the weather. Worth a closer look.

r5.title: {label}: tank at {pct} %
r5.detail: The modelled stock of “{name}” is around {stock} {unit} ({pct} % of capacity). A delivery should be scheduled.

r6.title: {label}: contract ends in {days} days
r6.detail: The contract “{provider}” ends in {days} days. Start a tariff comparison now and switch if needed.

r7.title: {label}: efficiency class {class} ({kwh} kWh/m²·a)
r7.detail: The heating energy demand {year} for {label} corresponds to efficiency class {class} ({kwh} kWh/m²·a). Insulation, heating optimisation or a hydraulic balance can improve the class noticeably.

tariff.title: Tariff comparison
tariff.subtitle: What would you have paid with a different tariff? Real contracts + hypothetical shadow contracts calculated on your actual consumption.
tariff.noUsable: No comparable utilities active. Tariff comparison applies to contract-based types (gas, electricity, district heating).
tariff.legend: Negative difference (green) = cheaper than the contract actually billed.

shadow.title: Create shadow contract
shadow.intro: A hypothetical tariff — does NOT affect balance/forecast, only this comparison.
shadow.label: Label
shadow.validation: Label, date and working price are required

analysis.title: 📊 Analysis

chartAlt.hdd: Scatter chart: consumption over heating degree days with regression models
chartAlt.years: Bar chart: consumption by year comparison

analysis.notTempDependent: {label} is not temperature-dependent — seasonal profile instead of HDD.
analysis.noAnomalies: No anomalies detected — all months are within the expected range (σ threshold from settings).
analysis.anomalyExplainHgt: Months whose consumption deviates from the HDD regression model by more than the σ threshold.
analysis.anomalyExplainSeasonal: Months whose consumption deviates from the seasonal profile by more than the σ threshold.

contractEnd.title: Contract end {stage}:
contractEnd.checkNote: Check the notice period and a follow-up contract.

yoy.title: Year comparison · monthly deltas
yoy.needTwo: At least two years with data needed — currently {count}.
yoy.note: Comparison only over months that have data in both years. Positive values = more consumption than the previous year.

spar.title: 💧 Water saving index
spar.bandGutNote: Consumption at or below the reference range.
spar.bandMittelNote: Consumption above the good band, but still below the warning threshold.
spar.bandWarnNote: Consumption clearly above the reference — check for saving potential.
spar.indexNote: {bandNote} Index 100 = exactly the per-person reference consumption stored in the settings.

forecast.title: 🔮 Forecast
forecast.chartAlt: Line chart: consumption history with forecast
forecast.info: Model: {model} · blend weight: {blend}%{r2} · last working price: {price} ct/{unit}
forecast.balanceLabel: Projected balance at the end of the horizon:
forecast.balanceNote: · cumulative from estimated costs minus projected advances
forecast.bonusNote: Future bonuses are not extrapolated — only bonuses recorded in the contract with a credit date within the forecast period are included in the costs.

report.title: Annual report {year}
report.noRecommendations: No open recommendations — everything looks good.
